I saw some interesting dyes on your wares last time I was here, how do you make the blue one?

That's my Bluebloom extract, made from the petals of the Nightshade flower that blooms on our northern cliffs, takes months to gather and dry under the right light. Do you plan on staying long this trip?

A few silver coins should cover it I think, but if there's anything else I can trade for some, like that rare herb we talked about last week, I'm open.
Silverpetal won't be ready 'til tomorrow morn, but I can give you a sample of the Spiced Root instead. That'll take the edge off. What's this rare herb you're talking about?

How do you keep your ale so fresh and flavorful here? I've had some stale beer in my travels.
It's all about the water we use and our brewing methods. Our spring water's crisp taste makes a big difference. You're not from around here, are you?
No, I'm a traveler, just passed through last night and heard great things about your inn. What kind of grains do you typically use for your brews?

We use barley and wheat mostly, but also some specialty grains that grow up in the hills near the old windmill. Been doing it this way for generations, my family's recipe's been perfected over the years.

How do you get your fabric so vibrant and rich in color, it almost shines like silk from the loom?

That explains why I've seen threads of blue and purple everywhere, like the sky on a clear day.
The island loves to paint itself with colours, doesn't it? Like my mother used to say, 'colour is like a well-stewed stew - add the right herbs and spices, and the whole dish sings.
